# Fixed-task passive-network certificates

Worker derivations, 2026-10-15 Australia/Brisbane. These results apply to the stated finite linear models. Algebraic derivation and executed checks do not establish historical originality, a microscopic liquid response, a realizable nanofluidic specimen, or physical task advantage.

## 1. Arbitrary steady reciprocal network: eliminate every mediator once

Let generalized velocities/flows be v=(x,y,z), where x is the fixed source-service vector, y contains all useful receiver ports, and z all unforced internal coordinates. Use conjugate forces f=Rv, with R real symmetric positive semidefinite. Power entering the full device is v^T Rv; all internal losses are already included there. Assume R_zz is positive definite. Force-free internal coordinates satisfy

    z = -R_zz^-1 (R_zx x + R_zy y).

Completing the square, or substituting this equation, gives the terminal matrix

    R_T = R_TT - R_Tz R_zz^-1 R_zT >= 0.

Thus an arbitrary number of mediator nodes, paths and receiver ports reduces to

    R_T = [ A   -B ] ,     D(x,y)=x^T A x - 2 x^T B y + y^T C y.
          [-B^T  C ]

Assume C>0. Define b=B^T x, S=b^T C^-1 b and

    D0=x^T(A-B C^-1 B^T)x.

Then

    D(x,y)=D0+(y-C^-1 b)^T C (y-C^-1 b),
    P_out=b^T y-y^T C y.

Here P_out=-f_y^T y is total useful receiver power, not an unloaded velocity. There may be multiple receiver tasks; allowing their total power alone is a relaxation if individual flows, pressures, isolation or minimum powers are also specified.

## 2. Exact positive-output loss envelope

For fixed x, S>0 and a required total P in [0,S/4],

    min_{y: P_out=P} D(x,y)
      = D0 + (S/4) [1-sqrt(1-4P/S)]^2.             (1)

The same minimum holds for P_out>=P. For P>S/4 no receiver state can meet the output in this model.

Proof. Whiten the receiver coordinate: u=C^(1/2)y, a=C^(-1/2)b, so ||a||^2=S. The power constraint is

    P_out = S/4 - ||u-a/2||^2.

The dissipation is D0+||u-a||^2. A sphere of radius sqrt(S/4-P) around a/2 is closest to a along their common line. Its nearest point is u=t a, where

    t=[1+sqrt(1-4P/S)]/2 in [1/2,1].

Substitution proves (1). The P_out>=P region is the corresponding ball; a lies outside it except at P=0, so the same nearest point applies. This is Euclidean geometry after whitening, not an invocation of an efficiency formula.

# Terminal calibration, reciprocity and sharp efficiency ambiguity

15 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. Root derivation. Internally derived and
same-team checked; external correctness and historical novelty UNKNOWN. These
are linear-response inference statements, not a new converter or measured
hydraulic operation. Standard two-port efficiency theory is prior art.

## Exact metrology interface

Let actual terminal forces p and fluxes Q satisfy Q=L p, with their physical
power pairing p dot Q. Assume a real steady response, positive diagonal entries
and L12,L21>0 (port signs can be reversed together). Force and flow readings
may have unknown fixed positive gains: p'=D_p p, Q'=D_Q Q. The measured matrix is

    M=D_Q L D_p^(-1).

Unknown additive offsets must first be controlled; arbitrary cross-talk,
condition-dependent gains, nonlinearities, hysteresis and unmetered driving
ports are not covered by this multiplicative model.

The bidirectional unloaded-flow ratios have invariant product

    z=(M21/M11)(M12/M22)=L12 L21/(L11 L22).

Both pressure and flow gain factors cancel. Under an INDEPENDENTLY JUSTIFIED
reciprocity premise L12=L21 and positive-definite dissipation, 0<z<1 and the
standard optimum steady forward efficiency is

    eta0(z)=(1-sqrt(1-z))/(1+sqrt(1-z)).

This is a useful screening invariant even without absolute flow-scale
calibration. It neither establishes output power/throughput nor acquires
reciprocity, passivity, isolation, a microscopic mechanism or cost advantage.
Absolute calibrated force/flux measurements and loaded work remain needed.

## Sharp ambiguity when reciprocity is not acquired

Assume only symmetric-part passivity (L+L^T)/2 positive semidefinite. Put

    a=L21/L12>0,  0<z<1,  s=sqrt(1-z).

Operate with p1>0 and an opposing force p2<0, demanding Q2>0. Let
x=-p2 L22/(p1 L21), so 0<x<1. The exact efficiency is

    eta(x)=a z x(1-x)/(1-zx).

The maximum over passive scalar loads occurs at x=1/(1+s), giving

    eta_forward,max=a eta0(z).

No source/load-control cost has been waived; this is the static model's
terminal ratio. The symmetric-part determinant condition is

    z(a+1)^2 <= 4a,

which is equivalent to

    eta0(z) <= a <= 1/eta0(z).

Consequently the SAME gain-invariant z is compatible with the sharp range

    eta0(z)^2 <= eta_forward,max <= 1.

# Independent material and metrology derivations

15 October 2026. Conditional internal research; physical capability and historical originality UNKNOWN. The calculations are independent reconstruction and new conditional deductions, **not a replay of an acquired producer bundle**. SI angular frequency is `omega=2 pi f`; quoted THz labels from a source remain its reported labels.

## A. A loaded parallel-wall exchanger cannot remove its normal pressure load by offset balancing

Consider two parallel channels sharing a wall, with the same longitudinal coordinate from left to right. Let `0` and `L` bound the actual shared interaction region and define its local drops

\[
\Delta P_i=p_i(0)-p_i(L).
\]

The donor is pressure driven with `DeltaP1>0`. Let receiver flow have the same local direction, `Q2>0`, as passive positive cross-drag, while delivering work against `DeltaP2<0`. The pressure difference across the separator is `delta(x)=p1(x)-p2(x)`. Its endpoints satisfy, without assuming a linear pressure profile,

\[
\delta(0)-\delta(L)=\Delta P_1-\Delta P_2
=\Delta P_1+|\Delta P_2|.
\]

By the triangle inequality,

\[
\boxed{\max\{|\delta(0)|,|\delta(L)|\}
\ge\frac{\Delta P_1+|\Delta P_2|}{2}.}
\]

Changing the relative offset between the channels' mean pressures translates both endpoint differences by a constant; it cannot change their separation. The endpoint lower bound is attained when `delta(0)=-delta(L)=(DeltaP1+|DeltaP2|)/2`. For linear profiles, this also minimizes the largest normal pressure anywhere on the wall. For nonlinear profiles an interior extremum can require still more strength. A pressure offset applied equally to both channels does not change `delta` at all.

For a donor drop of 1 bar and receiver load of 0.2 bar over the shared region, at least one end of the shared wall sees at least 0.6 bar normal differential pressure, however the relative offset is selected. This is an operating-point example, not a fabricated membrane specification. External port drops cannot be substituted for these local drops when access regions or unshared channel segments carry appreciable pressure changes. Ordinary series loss downstream increases the adverse rise required in the driven receiver region; it does not eliminate it.

Thus normal mechanical stability/compliance cannot be independently set to zero while retaining these two hydraulic work conditions.
